findings.title: Derived website_name bypasses untrusted attribute filtering
findings.body: `website_name` is added as a normal serialized attribute, but `website` is already in the `untrusted_attributes` list (lines 105-111), which suppresses fields for restricted users such as TL0 profiles viewed by anonymous visitors. Because `website_name` is derived from `website` and is not added to that untrusted list, it is still serialized and rendered when `website` itself would be hidden, leaking the user-supplied website host and path. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and add a spec asserting it is omitted alongside `website`.

findings.title: Inclusion predicate is missing the trailing question mark
findings.body: `include_website_name` is defined without the trailing `?`, while serializer inclusion predicates in this file follow the `include_email?` / `include_website_name?` convention. As written, this method is not used as the inclusion check, so `website_name` can be emitted even when `website` is blank (as a null field) instead of being omitted. Rename it to `def include_website_name?`.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain branch is not tested
findings.body: The new `website_name` serializer logic has distinct branches for exact host match, same-length subdomain siblings (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), and parent-domain suffix matching. The new examples cover exact host and parent-domain cases but not the sibling-subdomain `elsif` branch, so a regression in that branch would not fail these tests. Add a spec using two different subdomains of the same parent domain.
